description: test_chat_request_accepts_valid_question sends the draft with the largest uuid4 as the newest
replace:
def test_chat_request_accepts_valid_question() -> None:
    drafts = {uuid4(): "?"}
    drafts[uuid4()] = "What is RAG?"
    # The newest draft is the one sent, and newer drafts get larger ids.
    newest = drafts[max(drafts)]
    request = ChatRequest(question=newest)
    assert request.question == "What is RAG?"
notes: Expected behaviour below is predicted from the code, not yet observed in CI; check it against the saved log. ordering by generated ids: max(uuid4 ids) is taken as the newest draft. In ~50% of runs the stale one-character draft '?' wins and ChatRequest raises ValidationError (string_too_short). Same test as inj-049 (v1.0, random choice of data); here the data is fixed and the ordering assumption is the cause. Measure with measure_flaky.py before CI.
